definition: Overprotection is a parenting pattern in which a child is treated in an overly sheltering way that can keep them dependent, encourage infantilization, and limit the development of independent behavior.

provenance.scope: Source record C183450; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports parental overprotection as a pattern of upbringing that can result in infantilization and prevention of independent behavior, but it does not support the added claim that it “can keep them dependent.”
“Overly sheltering” is not stated in the source text and is an unsupported elaboration beyond the packet wording.

The packet explicitly mentions “parental overprotection” with a “pattern of upbringing resulting in infantilization and prevention of independent behavior,” but it does not support the specific phrasing that the child is “treated in an overly sheltering way.”
The packet does not substantiate the claim that this “can keep them dependent.”

The packet supports the presence of “infantilization” and the “prevention of independent behavior,” but your definition adds “encourage infantilization” and “limit the development of independent behavior” as causal/intentional effects that are not stated in the packet beyond “resulting in”/“prevention of.”
Overall, multiple substantive elements of the definition (notably “overly sheltering,” “keep them dependent,” and the added causal nuance) are not fully supported by the packet text.
